data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'ikh' which means 'to give' or 'gift'. In Islamic tradition, Ikha symbolizes the reward or gift bestowed upon one by Allah for their good deeds. The name Ikha carries the meaning “Gift, Reward” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ikha usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, reward and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ikha total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ikha holds a special meaning in Islamic culture as it is often used for children and signifies the hope and expectation that they will grow up to become righteous individuals who will be rewarded for their good deeds and actions. In many Muslim communities, the naming of a child as Ikha is seen as a way of invoking blessings and positive expectations for their future.
data.spiritual_significance: Ikha holds deep spiritual significance in Islam as it represents the concept of rewards and blessings bestowed upon individuals by Allah for their good deeds. It serves as a reminder of the idea that every action has a consequence, and that by striving to be good, kind, and compassionate, an individual may receive a great reward in this life and the next. The name Ikha therefore symbolizes the hope and aspiration for a righteous and virtuous life filled with blessings and divine favor.
